details.description: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is Google DeepMind's cost-efficient, low-latency model in the Gemini 3 series, described on its model card as based on Gemini 3 Pro and positioned for high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks such as translation, classification and data extraction. It is natively multimodal, accepting text, image, audio and video input over up to a 1,048,576-token context window, and supports function calling, code execution, structured outputs, and Google Search or Google Maps grounding. Google's developer documentation lists it as a Stable model, though Google's own Gemini overview page now promotes a newer Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite as its current recommendation for this performance tier.
advantages: Scores 86.9% on GPQA Diamond (scientific knowledge) and 88.9% on MMMLU (multilingual Q&A), per its Google DeepMind model card.
Scores 76.8% on MMMU-Pro and 84.8% on Video-MMMU for multimodal reasoning over images and video.
Scores 43.3% on SimpleQA Verified, a parametric-knowledge benchmark, and 72.0% on LiveCodeBench for code generation.
Supports function calling, code execution, structured outputs, and Google Search and Google Maps grounding, per Google's developer documentation.
disadvantages: Scores only 16.0% on Humanity's Last Exam, a difficult academic-reasoning benchmark, per its model card.
The model card defers its knowledge cutoff and detailed known-limitations to the Gemini 3 Pro model card rather than listing them directly.
Does not support audio generation, image generation, computer use, or the Live API, per Google's developer documentation.

Google's deprecations page lists an announced shutdown date of May 7, 2027 for this model, with gemini-3.5-flash-lite as the recommended replacement, and Google's Gemini overview page now promotes Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite as its current recommendation for high-volume, efficiency-focused tasks.
use_cases: High-volume, latency-sensitive tasks such as translation and classification, per its model card
Lightweight agentic workflows, data extraction and document processing, per Google's developer documentation
Long-context tasks such as summarizing large documents within its token context window
Tool-using workflows via function calling, code execution, and Google Search or Maps grounding

notes: Catalog's token limits (1,048,576 input / 65,536 output) match Google's developer docs (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.1-flash-lite) exactly. The model card states this model 'is based on Gemini 3 Pro' rather than a Flash-tier base model, and defers its knowledge cutoff and detailed limitations to the Gemini 3 Pro card, so no cutoff date is given here. Benchmark scores are read from the 'Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite High' column of the model card's comparison table (its highest thinking-effort setting), not the columns for sibling/competitor models shown alongside it; verified against the model card's own results image, all 8 cited scores match exactly. Catalog's modality list omits video input, which Google's docs also list as a supported input type for this model. Google's deprecations page confirms a shutdown date of May 7, 2027 for gemini-3.1-flash-lite, which matches the catalog's own deprecation_date fact exactly, with gemini-3.5-flash-lite listed as the recommended replacement.
